title: Compose and durably commit the provider-run record from the activation path
description:
Objective: close the last link between the landed telemetry producers and the landed durable sink, giving `buildProviderRunRecord`, `commitProviderRunRecord` and (transitively) `normalizeUsageMeasurement` their FIRST production call sites in apps/.

HARD DEPENDENCY: task-6c0db1f9920841fea295512f602054ee (Emit provider-run telemetry from the daemon activation path) must be DONE — this task consumes the `ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` that task produces. Re-measure it on disk before planning; a DONE status is not proof the symbol is reachable.

MEASURED GAP at HEAD ac09ca9, symbol by symbol. Both ends exist and nothing joins them:
- PRODUCER, landed and published: `buildProviderRunRecord` (packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/provider-run-record.ts:210, published at surface/provider-record-surface.ts:24). It internally calls `normalizeProviderUsage` (:238), which calls `@moe/scheduler`'s `normalizeUsageMeasurement` (provider-usage-normalization.ts:208; defined at packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-measurement.ts:210, published at scheduler/index.ts:115). So one call site here gives the scheduler's measurement authority its first transitive apps/ consumer too.
- SINK, landed 2026-08-16 by task-1a7ff170ee544a3a8a10962c25e2ca5b: `commitProviderRunRecord` (apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.ts:202) and `deriveProviderRunEventId` (:89), over the narrow `ProviderRunStore` port.
- THE GAP: `grep -rn "commitProviderRunRecord" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns ONLY its own definition. Zero callers. `buildProviderRunRecord` has zero apps/ hits. The ledger is a durable sink nothing writes to.

Deliverable: an activation-side composition step that takes the handoff from the prerequisite task, builds the record through `buildProviderRunRecord`, and commits it exactly once through `commitProviderRunRecord`, returning the commit result or an existing stable refusal.

NOT in scope: minting a record digest (the codec owns that — provider-run-codec.ts:156-162), re-normalizing usage (buildProviderRunRecord already does it), new store schema, budget decisions, benchmark harness, corpus, or scoring.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/activation/ or apps/daemon/src/telemetry/ (one new module + its .js bridge + its .test.ts). Do NOT publish from apps/daemon/src/index.ts; index-surface.test.ts pins EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length (85 at time of writing — re-measure, do not cite this number).

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code. Daemon gates are red at baseline from foreign in-flight slices; apply the path-attributed baseline over the owned paths.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "commitProviderRunRecord" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns a production call site OTHER than its own definition, and `grep -rn "buildProviderRunRecord" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns at least one — both counts were zero before this task.

A test against a REAL SqliteEventStore proves one activation produces exactly ONE committed provider-run event; a second identical activation is refused or replayed, asserting the exact stable code AND which layer answered (codec, ledger, or store — all three can refuse).
The record committed is the one `buildProviderRunRecord` returned, not a locally-composed lookalike: a mutation replacing the runner call with a hand-built object turns a NAMED test red.
No recordDigest is computed at this call site — the codec mints it; a test asserts the committed digest equals the codec's and a mutation supplying a local digest turns a NAMED test red.
A refusal at any layer leaves NO durable event: the test reads the aggregate back through the port and asserts it is empty, so a partial write cannot be reported as a refusal.
Each production source is under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, carries a physical one-line .js bridge, and apps/daemon/src/index.ts is unmodified.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately; the test leg prints a nonzero Test Files/Tests count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta intersected with the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Consume `buildProviderRunRecord` through the BARE specifier `@moe/runner` and `commitProviderRunRecord` through its daemon-local module. Do not reimplement record composition, usage normalization, digest minting, or commit authority — each already has exactly one owner.

NEVER call `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`; the narrow `ProviderRunStore` port deliberately cannot name them, because `CommitApply` hands out a raw DatabaseSync and the no-new-schema rail forbids it. Verify the port still omits them.
Real SqliteEventStore in tests, opened per test and closed in a `finally` on every exit path — a held handle kills the vitest worker.
Fail closed: an unobservable or refused run produces no durable event and stays UNKNOWN. A partial write reported as a refusal is a defect, not an acceptable outcome.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE, AND TAKE THE COMMITTABILITY DECISION — the reopenReason demands it be decided and pinned, so it is settled here rather than left to the worker.
LANDED PREREQUISITE, re-measured at HEAD 0f19e06: `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.ts` (97 lines) exports `launchActivationProviderRun(input): Promise<ClaudeTelemetryLaunchResult>` (:90), `ActivationTelemetryLaunchInput` (:72), and `ActivationProviderRunIdentity` (:59) — the five keying facts `{provider:"claude", runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch}`. It returns the runner's result UNCHANGED, deliberately, so the UNKNOWNs survive.
COMPOSITION TARGETS, re-confirm each: `buildProviderRunRecord` (packages/runner/.../provider-run-record.ts:210, published at surface/provider-record-surface.ts:24); `commitProviderRunRecord` (apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.ts:202); `deriveProviderRunEventId` (:89); `ProviderRunCommitInput` = `{correlationId, decidedAt, key: CommandDecisionKey, record: unknown, requestBytes}` (:63) — `record` is `unknown` BY DESIGN, "the codec is the only authority on what is a record"; `ProviderRunCommitResult` = `{ok:true, aggregateId, digest, disposition: "COMMITTED"|"REPLAYED", record}` | `ProviderRunRefusal` (:72-80).
THE DECISION. `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` has three outcomes, not two:
(1) `ok:false` — reachable ONLY for a malformed run ref (`TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` at `TELEMETRY_INPUT`). **DO NOT COMMIT.** There is no valid five-fact identity, so `deriveProviderRunEventId` has nothing to key on and no aggregate exists. Return the refusal unchanged.
(2) `ok:true` with a BLIND handoff — launcher refused, or nothing attempted; facts UNKNOWN, `telemetryRefusal` populated. **COMMIT IT.** Epic rail 4 says missing or unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority — it does NOT say it goes unrecorded. A committed record whose `terminal` and `infrastructure` read UNKNOWN is an honest record of an unobservable run; withholding it instead leaves the ledger unable to distinguish a refused launch from a launch that never happened, which is the evidence gap the benchmark harness (task-b937811e) exists to close.
(3) `ok:true` OBSERVED — commit normally.
So the durable falsehood the reopenReason warns about is NOT "committing a blind handoff". It is committing one AS IF OBSERVED. `buildProviderRunRecord` already maps blind handoffs to UNKNOWN facts, so committing preserves the truth; step 2 asserts nothing can read such a record as a success.
GATES, each run separately with its own exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, recording the count line and every failing file as your before-set. Both expected RED from foreign slices; repair none of it.

GAP CONFIRMED OPEN, both greps: `commitProviderRunRecord` non-test in apps returns ONLY provider-run-ledger.ts:202 (its own definition); `buildProviderRunRecord` non-test in apps returns ONLY provider-run-ledger.ts:9, a COMMENT. Zero real callers of either.

PREREQUISITE RE-MEASURED ON DISK, not trusted from status: apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.ts, 97 lines, exports launchActivationProviderRun (:90), ActivationTelemetryLaunchInput (:72), ActivationProviderRunIdentity (:59). Returns the runner's ClaudeTelemetryLaunchResult unchanged.

=== DEVIATION FINDING 1 (material; step 4 as written cannot compile) ===
THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT `ProviderRunRecord` TYPES AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. The plan assumed buildProviderRunRecord's output can be handed straight to commitProviderRunRecord. It cannot; the codec would refuse EVERY such record.
- runner ProviderRunRecord (provider-run-record.ts:97) keys: recordVersion, provider, identity, model, observedModel, decisionDigests, runtimeEvidence, startedAt, completedAt, terminal, infrastructure, tokens, steps, concurrency, usage (a ProviderUsageResult object), telemetryRefusal.
- daemon ProviderRunRecord (provider-run-contracts.ts:94) keys: recordVersion, providerRunRef, launch, declared, observedModel, terminal, infrastructure, tokens, steps, sequence, concurrency, observedStart, observedEnd, usage (a dense NormalizedMeasurement ARRAY), usageRefusals, upstreamRefusal, stdoutReceiptDigest, stderrReceiptDigest, recordDigest.
- The codec's admission list is hard: provider-run-codec.validation.ts:30-34 REQUIRED_KEYS demands providerRunRef, launch, declared, sequence, usageRefusals, stdoutReceiptDigest, stderrReceiptDigest — none of which the runner record has — so validateProviderRunRecordShape returns "RECORD" and encodeProviderRunRecord refuses PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_MALFORMED at the codec layer. Also steps is {count,coverage} in the runner vs {turns,coverage} in the daemon.
RESOLUTION, keeping the objective intact and reimplementing no authority: the daemon record is a PROJECTION of the handoff (providerRunRef, launch, declared, observedModel, terminal, infrastructure, tokens, steps, sequence, concurrency, stdoutReceiptDigest, stderrReceiptDigest, upstreamRefusal=telemetryRefusal all travel VERBATIM from ClaudeTelemetryHandoff), and buildProviderRunRecord is the sole source of the one field the handoff does NOT carry — normalized `usage`, via its internal normalizeProviderUsage -> @moe/scheduler normalizeUsageMeasurement. So buildProviderRunRecord stays load-bearing and gets its real first apps/ call site; DoD 3's drill becomes "replace the runner call with a hand-built usage/refusal projection" and must redden a named test.

=== DEVIATION FINDING 2 (DoD 4's drill is an equivalent mutant as written) ===
"a mutation supplying a local digest turns a NAMED test red" is unsatisfiable literally: provider-run-codec.ts:152-157 strips recordDigest via withoutDigest BEFORE digesting and then overwrites it, so a caller-supplied digest is provably unobservable. Killable replacement, asserted on the production surface: the composition emits recordDigest "" (no local opinion) and a named test pins that, so computing one locally reddens; separately the committed digest is asserted equal to the digest decoded from the DURABLE event payload.

=== DEVIATION FINDING 3 (step 2c OBSERVED arm unreachable) ===
Re-verified independently, not taken from memory: grep over packages/runner/src/index.ts + surface/*.ts finds prepareClaudeRuntimePin, registerLaunchLock, resolveDuplicateDelivery, intakeProcessObservation and CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_DEFAULTS ONLY inside comments — zero exports — and claude-launcher.ts uses `entry.deps ?? CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_DEFAULTS`, all-or-nothing. So reaching the OBSERVED arm from apps/** requires spawning a real claude.exe, and minting a handoff by hand is reimplementing withheld runner authority (snapshotRunRef/unknownFact/telemetryRefusal are all internal). Disclosed, not silently narrowed; the same disclosure was made and QA-ACCEPTED on the prerequisite task-6c0db1f9. Blind arms (REFUSED, NOT_ATTEMPTED) and the ok:false malformed-ref arm remain fully reachable and are what the tests drive.

=== COMMITTABILITY DECISION, PINNED AS THE PLAN REQUIRES ===
(1) ok:false (TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED at TELEMETRY_INPUT, the only route) -> DO NOT COMMIT, return unchanged, no invented identity, aggregate stays empty.
(2) ok:true BLIND (TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED / TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_A

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 1 — pin the three arms of the committability decision. Create the module's test against the not-yet-existing composition and let it fail to resolve. Then:
(a) MALFORMED RUN REF -> the launch's `ok:false` is returned unchanged with `TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` at `TELEMETRY_INPUT`, and NOTHING is written: read the aggregate back through the ledger's port and assert it is empty. Committing here is impossible anyway — there is no valid identity — so the assertion is that the code does not try and does not invent one.
(b) BLIND HANDOFF -> a record IS committed, and its `terminal` and `infrastructure` read UNKNOWN with `telemetryRefusal` populated, read back from the durable bytes rather than from the in-memory value. Cover BOTH blind shapes separately — `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` and `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED` — and assert they remain distinguishable in the committed record; collapsing them loses which happened.
(c) OBSERVED -> a record is committed carrying the runner's real facts.
THEN THE ASSERTION THAT MAKES (b) SAFE: no committed blind record can be read as a success. Assert across the whole file that a record whose facts are UNKNOWN never presents a truth class above UNKNOWN and never carries a terminal outcome that a consumer could mistake for a completed run. This is what separates "honest record of an unobservable run" from "durable falsehood", and it is the reason (b) is committable at all.
Every refusal assertion pins the exact stable code AND the answering layer — the codec, the ledger and the store can each refuse, so a code-only assertion detaches the moment a different one answers first. Build each fixture valid at the earlier layers so the intended one speaks.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED confirmed: `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-run-commit.test.ts` from apps/daemon EXIT=1, "Cannot find module './activation-run-commit.js'", `Test Files 1 failed (1)`.

THE THREE ARMS ARE PINNED. (a) malformed run ref: asserts the launch's ok:false object is returned BY IDENTITY (`toBe(launch)`, so it cannot be re-wrapped), code TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED at layer TELEMETRY_INPUT, plus `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS` does NOT contain that layer — so a re-coding into this family reddens. Nothing durable: readEvents empty on BOTH the well-formed aggregate AND the aggregate derived from the malformed ref (that second read is the "did not invent an identity" assertion), and getCommandDecision(KEY) is null so no decision was recorded either. (b) BLIND: both shapes covered separately and asserted DISTINGUISHABLE field by field — REFUSED gives terminal REFUSED / infrastructure LAUNCH_REFUSED / launch.kind REFUSED / upstreamRefusal TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED; NOT_ATTEMPTED gives UNKNOWN / LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED / EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH / TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED; all read from the DURABLE bytes via decodeProviderRunRecord over store.readEvents, never from the in-memory value. (c) OBSERVED: absent, disclosed in the file header with the measurement, not silently narrowed.

THE SAFETY CONDITION IS FILE-WIDE, not per case: `assertNeverReadsAsSuccess(record)` runs on every committed record — upstreamRefusal non-null, terminal never COMPLETED, infrastructure never NONE, launch.observationDigest/startedAt/completedAt null, tokens.inputTokens and steps.turns and sequence carry NO `value` property (an unmeasured count must never arrive as a measured zero), observedModel.snapshotKind UNKNOWN, usage empty.

NEW FINDING, and it is what makes DoD 3 satisfiable at all. `buildProviderRunRecord`'s ONLY contribution to the daemon record is normalized `usage`, and on EVERY arm reachable from apps/** normalizeProviderUsage refuses at its FIRST guard (provider-usage-normalization.ts:184, startedAt/completedAt null on a blind handoff) before any row exists — so the usage projection is constant-empty on all reachable arms and an omitted runner call would be behaviourally invisible to any usage-equality assertion. Priors are unreachable too: the interval guard runs before the priors guard at :193. So the runner call is instead proven ON THE PATH by a case that only it can answer: a structurally broken handoff makes `buildProviderRunRecord` throw inside `launchUnknown` (provider-run-record.ts:137-142 reads telemetryRefusal first), which the composition converts to PROVIDER_RUN_HANDOFF_MALFORMED at PROVIDER_RUN_COMPOSITION. A locally-composed lookalike would sail past and be answered by the CODEC with PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_MALFORMED at PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC instead — a different code at a different layer, so the assertion reddens. Drill 3-equivalent is scheduled in step 5.

RESERVED VOCABULARY CONFIRMED UNUSED BEFORE THIS TASK: grep shows PROVIDER_RUN_COMPOSITION, PROVIDER_RUN_HANDOFF_MALFORMED, PROVIDER_RUN_USAGE_SEQUENCE_INVALID and PROVIDER_RUN_MEASUREMENT_REFUSED appear ONLY in provider-run-refusals.ts and its own test — the layer's doc comment names it "the composition before any record exists", i.e. this module. So the codes are used as designed, not invented.

DIGEST PROVENANCE, reworked per step-1 finding 2 into something actually killable: the composition emits `recordDigest: ""` and a named test pins that (`mints no record digest — the codec is the only authority on it`), plus the durable record's recordDigest is asserted equal to the ledger's returned digest and to a 64-hex shape. Supplying a local digest is provably unobservable through the codec (it strips the key before digesting), so the assertion had to move onto the composition's own output.

All fixtures are valid at the earlier layers: the REFUSED arm is reached through a real production model-mismatch refusal rather than a malformed request, and the NOT_ATTEMPTED arm drives the REAL resolveDuplicateDelivery via `{claim, registration:null, lockState:"RELEASED", effectState:"ACTIVE"}`.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — replay and atomicity, against a REAL SqliteEventStore opened per test and closed in a `finally` on every exit path (a held handle kills the vitest worker).
REPLAY: the ledger answers `disposition: "COMMITTED" | "REPLAYED"`. Commit one activation, then re-run the SAME identity and assert the second answers REPLAYED and that the durable aggregate still holds exactly ONE event. Then the case that actually kills the echo defect: re-run the same identity with a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT handoff and assert the answer carries the FIRST record's bytes, read back from the aggregate — not the second's. The store's replay identity does not cover the events array (see activation-ledger-commit.ts:12-24), so a replay answered from the caller's own record makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and pass forever.
ATOMICITY: a refusal at ANY layer leaves NO durable event. For each refusal arm — malformed ref, codec refusal, store refusal — read the aggregate back and assert it is empty or unchanged, never a fragment. A partial write reported as a refusal is a defect, not an acceptable outcome.
DIGEST PROVENANCE: assert the committed `digest` is the codec's, and that this call site computes none of its own. `provider-run-codec.ts:156-162` mints `recordDigest` over the canonical record with the field excluded, then seals — so the ledger's returned digest is the only authority and a locally-computed one would be a second, drifting opinion.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED PART 2 written; still unresolvable (module absent), so the whole file stays red. Real SqliteEventStore opened per `it` via SqliteEventStore.openEphemeralForProjectTest and closed in a `finally` on every exit path — nine stores, nine finallys, no shared handle.

REPLAY, three cases. (1) Identical resubmit: same key, same requestBytes, same run identity -> first COMMITTED, second REPLAYED, second.digest === first.digest, aggregate still exactly ONE event. (2) THE ECHO KILLER, `answers a changed-byte resubmit from the DURABLE record, never the caller's`: same key and same requestBytes but a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT handoff — first commit is the REFUSED arm, resubmit is the NOT_ATTEMPTED arm, which differ in terminal, infrastructure, launch.kind and upstreamRefusal.code. The store's replay identity omits the events array (it hashes key, commandKind, targetAggregateId, expectedVersion, requestBytes), so the store replays cleanly while the record describes a run nobody committed; the ledger's own cross-check must answer PROVIDER_RUN_REPLAY_DIVERGED at PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER with storeCode null (this ledger refusing, not the store), and the durable aggregate must still decode to the FIRST record — terminal REFUSED, infrastructure LAUNCH_REFUSED, upstreamRefusal TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED. A caller-echoing replay returns ok:true here and reddens. (3) Distinct command on a committed run — different commandId AND different requestBytes so it is not a replay at all — must answer PROVIDER_RUN_EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT at PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER with the aggregate unchanged at one event still holding the first record.

ATOMICITY on every refusal arm, each reading the aggregate BACK rather than trusting the return value: malformed run ref (arm a, step 2) -> zero events on both the well-formed and the malformed-derived aggregate id, and getCommandDecision null; composition refusal (handoff-malformed) -> zero events, decision null; CODEC refusal -> zero events, decision null; STORE refusal -> zero events.

THE CODEC ARM IS REACHED WITHOUT PLANTING ANYTHING. The daemon's clock readings are the only caller-supplied part of this record, so `{serverWallSeconds:-1, bootId:"", monotonicObservation:1.5}` fails the validator's `clock()` predicate (count/nonempty/count) and the codec answers PROVIDER_RUN_FIELD_INVALID at PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC. The composition deliberately does NOT pre-validate the clock — a daemon-side check would be validating one record while the codec digests another — so this case also pins that the codec, not the composition, is the shape authority.

THE STORE ARM uses the narrow ProviderRunStore port with commit delegating to a thrown `new DurableStoreError("STORE_INPUT_INVALID","refused")` while getCommandDecision and readEvents stay the REAL store, so the empty-aggregate read-back is genuine. Asserts PROVIDER_RUN_FIELD_INVALID at PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER with storeCode preserved VERBATIM as "STORE_INPUT_INVALID" — pinning the ledger's deliberate choice that an input fault is ours and never "unavailable", and pinning that the upstream code is not flattened into ours.

FOUR DISTINCT LAYERS ARE NOW SEPARATELY ASSERTED across the file — TELEMETRY_INPUT (launcher), PROVIDER_RUN_COMPOSITION, PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC, PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER — so no assertion can silently detach onto a different refusing layer.

DIGEST PROVENANCE pinned in step 2's `mints no record digest` case: composition emits recordDigest "", durable recordDigest === ledger digest === /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT THE COMPOSITION. Create `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-run-commit.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./activation-run-commit.ts";`, LF ending — apps/daemon requires a physical bridge per production module and the guard byte-compares, so CRLF or a trailing blank line lands it in `wrongContent`).
Flow: take the launch result from `launchActivationProviderRun` plus the commit envelope facts. On `ok:false`, return it unchanged — no commit, no invented identity. On `ok:true`, call `buildProviderRunRecord(handoff, context)` from the BARE specifier `@moe/runner`, then `commitProviderRunRecord` once with `ProviderRunCommitInput`. Return the ledger's `ProviderRunCommitResult` with its code and layer intact.
DO NOT re-normalize usage: `buildProviderRunRecord` already calls `normalizeProviderUsage` (provider-run-record.ts:238), which reaches `@moe/scheduler`'s `normalizeUsageMeasurement` — landing this call site is also what gives that its first transitive apps/ consumer, so a second normalization here would both duplicate work and create a competing measurement.
DO NOT compute a `recordDigest`: the codec mints it. Pass the record through as `unknown` — `ProviderRunCommitInput.record` is typed that way deliberately, "the codec is the only authority on what is a record", so a daemon-side pre-validation would be checking one record and committing another.
NEVER call `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`. The narrow `ProviderRunStore` port deliberately cannot name them because `CommitApply` hands out a raw `DatabaseSync` and the no-new-schema rail forbids it — verify the port still omits them.
Keep the module under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). Do NOT publish from apps/daemon/src/index.ts — index-surface.test.ts pins an exact export count and index.ts is not an owned path here.

GREEN. `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-run-commit.ts` created, 246 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (under 250), plus the one-line LF bridge `activation-run-commit.js` verified byte-wise with `od -c`: ends `. t s " ; \n`, no CRLF, no trailing blank. apps/daemon/src/index.ts UNMODIFIED — nothing published from the root, so index-surface.test.ts's pinned export count is untouched.

Focused run from apps/daemon: `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-run-commit.test.ts` -> EXIT=0, count line `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 12 passed (12)`. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT=0.

SURFACE: `composeProviderRunRecord(handoff, clock, priors?)` -> `{ok:true, record}` | ProviderRunRefusal, and `commitActivationProviderRun(store, input)` -> ProviderRunCommitResult | ProviderTelemetryRefusal. Composition is exported separately so its output is assertable directly, which is what makes the digest-provenance and usage-provenance assertions land on the production surface rather than on a test helper.

THE PROJECTION, forced by step-1 finding 1 and documented in the module header. Twelve fields travel VERBATIM from the handoff — providerRunRef, launch, declared, observedModel, terminal, infrastructure, tokens, steps, sequence, concurrency, stdoutReceiptDigest, stderrReceiptDigest — plus upstreamRefusal = handoff.telemetryRefusal and the caller's two ClockObservations. `buildProviderRunRecord` is called through the BARE specifier `@moe/runner` and contributes the one fact the handoff does not carry: normalized `usage`, and with it the first transitive apps/ consumer of @moe/scheduler's normalizeUsageMeasurement. Only `.usage` is read from the runner's record because every other field of it is a differently-shaped restatement of handoff facts; taking both would create two spellings of one fact inside durable bytes.

USAGE PROJECTION RULES, each with a reason rather than a default: a normalized result yields its measurements; a USAGE_INPUT refusal (no interval, no sequence, no readable receipt) yields empty usage and NO invented envelope refusal, because each of those is already visible in the record's own UNKNOWN fields; PROVIDER_USAGE_PRIOR_UNREADABLE is the one USAGE_INPUT code that refuses at PROVIDER_RUN_COMPOSITION with PROVIDER_RUN_MEASUREMENT_REFUSED, because it is a fault in CALLER data that is invisible in the record and committing empty usage for it would report an unmeasured run that was measurable; a USAGE_AUTHORITY refusal is carried as a real usageRefusals envelope with its exact LayeredIssues, guarded by PROVIDER_RUN_USAGE_SEQUENCE_INVALID rather than defaulting providerSequence to 0 if the sequence is ever unknown there.

CRASH IS NOT A REFUSAL: the buildProviderRunRecord call is wrapped so a handoff it cannot read becomes PROVIDER_RUN_HANDOFF_MALFORMED at PROVIDER_RUN_COMPOSITION instead of an escaping TypeError. This is a crash guard, NOT a second validator — nothing here inspects the record's shape, and the clock facts (the only caller data in the record) are deliberately passed unvalidated so the codec stays the sole shape authority.

RAILS HELD: no recordDigest computed (emits ""), no second normalization, no pre-validation of the record, record passed through as `unknown`. `grep -n "commitWithApply\|commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply"` over the new module and over provider-run-contracts.ts returns nothing — the ProviderRunStore port still names only commitExpectedVersionDecision, getCommandDecision and readEvents, so neither could be reached even by accident. The uncommittable arm is returned BY IDENTITY (`return input.launch`), which the test pins with `toBe`.

WORKTREE NOTE for the drills: all three of my files are UNTRACKED, so `git checkout -- <path>` cannot restore them (no HEAD blob). Byte snapshots are taken outside the repo before each drill and restored by copy, with sha256 re-verified after.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS — prove the decision and the replay answer are load-bearing. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) THE REPLAY-ECHO DRILL: switch the replay answer to echo the caller's record instead of the durable one; the changed-byte replay case from step 3 MUST redden. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Commit ONLY observed handoffs; refuse on blind ones. REJECTED after weighing it against the downstream consumer, and it is the tempting reading of "do not write falsehoods". It leaves no durable trace of a refused launch, so the ledger cannot distinguish "refused" from "never happened" — exactly the gap the benchmark harness needs closed. Drill 3 exists because this is the natural over-correction.

2) Commit everything including `ok:false`. REJECTED: a malformed run ref means there are no five identity facts, so `deriveProviderRunEventId` cannot key a record and any commit would require synthesising an identity the run never had. Drill 2 guards it.

3) Collapse the two blind shapes (`TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` and `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`) into one committed "unknown" record. REJECTED: they are different facts — the launcher refused before any bytes existed, versus this delivery launched no process at all — and the ledger is the only place that distinction survives.

4) Pre-validate the record before committing. REJECTED: `ProviderRunCommitInput.record` is typed `unknown` deliberately because the codec is the sole authority. A daemon-side validation would check one record and commit another.

5) Compute the digest here for a simpler commit envelope. REJECTED: the codec mints it with the field excluded from its own digest domain, so a locally-computed digest is a second, drifting opinion about the same bytes.

6) Re-normalize usage at this call site for explicitness. REJECTED: `buildProviderRunRecord` already does it, and a second pass would produce a competing measurement over one run.

7) Answer a replay from the caller's record to avoid the extra store read. REJECTED — it is THE defect that ships green here, since the store's replay identity does not cover the events array.

That last clause is what makes this task's decision possible.

COMPOSITION TARGETS, all present: `buildProviderRunRecord` (runner provider-run-record.ts:210, published provider-record-surface.ts:24); `commitProviderRunRecord` (provider-run-ledger.ts:202); `deriveProviderRunEventId` (:89); `ProviderRunCommitInput` = `{correlationId, decidedAt, key, record: unknown, requestBytes}` (:63) with `record` unknown by design — "the codec is the only authority on what is a record"; `ProviderRunCommitResult` = `{ok:true, aggregateId, digest, disposition:"COMMITTED"|"REPLAYED", record}` | refusal (:72-80). `ProviderRunRecord` carries `terminal` (:108) and `infrastructure` (:109), which are the fields that distinguish an observed run from a blind one.

THE COMMITTABILITY DECISION, settled here because the reopenReason requires it pinned. `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` has THREE outcomes, not two:
- `ok:false` reaches only from a malformed run ref (`TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` at `TELEMETRY_INPUT`). NOT committable — without the five identity facts `deriveProviderRunEventId` has nothing to key on and no aggregate exists. Return the refusal.
- `ok:true` BLIND (launcher refused / nothing attempted; facts UNKNOWN, `telemetryRefusal` populated). COMMITTABLE. Epic rail 4 says unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority — it does not say it goes unrecorded. A record whose terminal/infrastructure read UNKNOWN is an honest record of an unobservable run.
- `ok:true` OBSERVED. Committable normally.

WHY BLIND IS COMMITTABLE, which is the part worth arguing rather than asserting: withholding blind records leaves the ledger unable to distinguish a refused launch from a launch that never happened. That is precisely the evidence gap task-b937811e (benchmark telemetry harness) exists to close, and it is blocked on this wire. The durable falsehood the reopenReason warns about is not "committing a blind handoff" — it is committing one AS IF OBSERVED. `buildProviderRunRecord` already maps blind handoffs to UNKNOWN facts, so committing preserves the truth; the safety condition is the assertion that no blind record can be read as a success, which step 2 pins and drill 4 proves.

REPLAY HAZARD carried from the ledger's own planning: the store's replay identity does NOT cover the events array (activation-ledger-commit.ts:12-24). A replay answered with the caller's record makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes. Only the changed-byte replay case kills it.

DIGEST: `provider-run-codec.ts:156-162` mints `recordDigest` over the canonical record with the field excluded, then seals. This call site computes none.

NORMALIZATION: `buildProviderRunRecord` calls `normalizeProviderUsage` (:238), which reaches `@moe/scheduler`'s `normalizeUsageMeasurement`. Landing this call site gives that its first transitive apps/ consumer — a second normalization here would duplicate work and create a competing measurement.
